title: Audit Your Own MLOps Pipeline Before It Silently Lies to You

sections.title: Count Your Real Traffic
sections.prompt: Pull your actual prediction volume for the last 7 days (from logs, a database table, or an API gateway dashboard) and divide by 7 to get predictions/day. Write that number down next to a one-line note on what infrastructure you're currently running (Kubernetes, managed endpoint, cron job) and decide honestly whether the machinery matches the number.

sections.title: Find Your Own Relative-Path Trap
sections.prompt: Grep your training and serving code for every place a path, config value, or environment variable is set without an absolute path or explicit env var (like MLflow's `./mlruns` default). List each one, then write the one-line assert that would catch it firing from the wrong working directory, following the pattern in the post's `ARTIFACT_ROOT` example.

sections.title: Rewrite Your Cron Line
sections.prompt: Open your actual crontab (or systemd timer unit) for any scheduled training or retraining job and check it against the two rules from the post: full path to your venv's Python binary, and a MAILTO or webhook on failure. Rewrite the line to fix whichever is missing, and test it once with `run-parts` or manually invoking it from `$HOME` to confirm it still resolves correctly.

sections.title: Pick Your Tool Swaps
sections.prompt: Go through your current stack orchestrator, tracking, serving, monitoring, and for each one you're paying for or over-provisioning, name the free swap from the post (Prefect for Airflow, self-hosted MLflow for a capped free tier, FastAPI+Uvicorn for a managed endpoint, Evidently for Arize/Fiddler) and estimate the monthly dollar difference.

sections.title: Decide What You're Allowed to Skip
sections.prompt: List one monitoring or safety check you're currently skipping (or tempted to skip), like the post's Parquet-log-instead-of-Evidently choice on a low-stakes home project, and write the specific condition that would force you to build it for real (e.g. 'the day a bad prediction costs a customer, not just a squint at a chart').

cta: Run the relative-path grep from section 2 on your own repo and reply with what you found — even a clean result is worth reporting.
